title: merchant-integration-sampler-scratchpad
content:
Working notes for Merchant integration outreach (scratchpad)

Context / quick summary:
- Target: mid-market payment processor / fintech platform (placeholder name: Merchant Sampler)
- Why they matter: large volume of low-latency inference for payment-UX features (fraud hints, message personalization, merchant-facing recon), sensitive data (PII + transactional), likely want predictable cost and an on-prem/VPC option.
- Hypothesis: primary friction is ops + security; secondary is cost predictability and latency at scale.

Account research (what I pulled together):
- Core product: payment routing + merchant dashboards, ~40M tx/mo, peak bursts in regionally-concentrated hours.
- Tech stack: mostly Kubernetes on AWS, some customers on dedicated VMs. Integrations via webhooks and REST.
- Procurement: procurement + security review required for vendor with access to transaction metadata.
- Likely decision makers: Head of Platform (Katie R), Head of Payments (Devon M), Sec/Compliance (legal reviewer).
- Signals: recent hiring for infra reliability, published blog about latency SLAs, RFP posted (private) — good window for outreach.

Value props to emphasize (short bullets for use in emails/pitches):
- Predictable unit economics: reserved/dedicated capacity options + cost tooling to forecast per-transaction inference cost.
- Latency-first runtime: continuous batching + KV caching to keep tail P95 latency low for short prompts (fraud hint scenarios).
- Private deployment available (VPC or on-prem) for regulated data + KMS integration; audit logs and HIPAA-like controls.
- Smooth dev ergonomics: same API/SDK across hosted/dedicated/private, simple rollout controls (canary, fallback to smaller/cheaper model).
- Ops lift reduction vs self-hosting: we manage kernel selection, autoscaling policies and GPU orchestration.

Outbound subject line ideas (A/B test):
- Quick question on reducing per-transaction inference cost
- Can Redwood reduce your fraud-ML latency by 30%?
- Pilot: private LLM inference for payment UX (no data leaves VPC)

Cold email draft — version A (concise):
Hi {FirstName},

Noticed Merchant Sampler is doubling transactions and prioritizing latency in product posts. We help payments teams run LLM inference with predictable costs and private deployments (VPC/on-prem) so sensitive transaction data never leaves your environment.

If you have 20 minutes I can share a short pilot plan (4 weeks, measurable cost & latency targets) and a checklist for security review.

— Maya (Redwood Inference)

Cold email draft — version B (more explicit metrics / pilot):
Subject: 4-week pilot: private LLM inference for payments

Hi {FirstName},

We partner with mid-market payment platforms to replace brittle self-hosted model endpoints and reduce per-transaction inference costs by combining caching, batching, and quantized model variants. Typical pilot: 4 weeks, we deploy a VPC-controlled private runtime, run a small traffic slice, and measure p50/p95 latency + $/inference. No model ownership changes required — you can pin model versions.

Do you have time next week for a quick technical sync?

— Maya

LinkedIn message (short):
Hey {FirstName} — I work on integrations for Redwood Inference. We do private/VPC LLM inference for payments teams. Would love 10 minutes to share a pilot plan if you’re evaluating vendors.

Call pitch (30s):
- Quick intro: Redwood Inference = inference platform (hosted/dedicated/private) focused on production economics.
- Problem: self-hosting = ops overhead + unpredictable costs; hosted-only = data residency concerns.
- Ask: 20–30 min technical intro with infra + sec to explore pilot.

Anticipated objections + suggested responses:
- "We already use OpenAI / hosted APIs":
  - Response: many teams use hosted models for development; for production we offer reserved capacity and private deployments that keep data in your VPC + SLA-backed latency and throughput. We also provide tooling that reduces token spend (prefix caching, batching) so unit costs drop.
- "We can self-host — we don't need a platform":
  - Response: self-hosting crews up time & SRE effort. We manage kernel selection, quantization profiles, autoscaling, and GPU orchestration — typically saves 2–4 FTE months and prevents regex-level regressions in tail latency.
- "Security/compliance concerns":
  - Response: show the security pack: VPC private control plane, KMS integrations, audit logs, SOC2 scope, and we can do a security technical deep-dive. Offer to map their checklist to our controls.
- "Price is unclear":
  - Response: propose a short pilot with defined success metrics. For pilots we give transparent cost modeling and a sample forecast: expected $/inference range + options to move to reserved commit for predictability.

Pilot proposal (single paragraph):
- 4-week technical pilot: deploy Redwood Private in a VPC with a small reserved pool (2 x T4-equivalent) and route 5–10% of a traffic slice to test fraud-hint and merchant messaging flows. Deliverables: latency/cost baseline vs pilot, integration playbook, security checklist mapping, and decision recommendations (scale vs. rollback).

Request checklist for initial call (prep):
- Basic infra contacts + Slack channel (infra, sec, product).
- Sample traffic shape (per-minute and per-hour distribution).
- Example prompts / sizes used in fraud hints & messages.
- Compliance requirements doc (if any): SOC2, PCI, regional constraints.
- Who owns procurement signing? timeline expectations?

Open questions for discovery (notes to self):
- How many transactions are stateful/require KV caching vs stateless?
- Are there any customer contracts that forbid sending transaction metadata to third-party cloud? (If yes, escalate private/on-prem.)
- What are their current p95 latency targets for real-time features?
- Which models/architectures are they currently experimenting with? (OpenAI, Llama variants, internal models)

Next steps / TODO:
- Craft tailored email for Devon M + Katie R with 1-paragraph value prop and pilot ask (due: 2026-03-08).
- Ask solutions engineer (Priya) for sample pilot config + placeholder cost model (action: ping in Slack).
- Prepare security one-pager mapping to typical payments checklist (owner: Omar, due 2026-03-10).
- Draft an internal 15-minute demo flow showing latency improve & cost forecast for merchant messaging.
- Add a short playbook for legal/procurement handoffs (template).

Notes-to-self (rough):
- Keep initial outreach lightweight — emphasize security and cost predictability, not model accuracy.
- If they ask about model explainability, reply with our eval tool and logs + plan to run small eval on their prompt set.
- Consider referencing similar (anonymized) pilot: 'regional-payments-co' (reduced inference $/tx by ~25% in pilot) — check with solutions for approval to mention.

Random brainstorm angles (throwaway):
- Productized starter: 'Payments inference quickstart' — 1-click config for webhook mapping, sample prompts, preapproved sec controls, 2-week rollout. Could be a small GTM asset.
- Co-marketing: joint webinar on 'LLMs in payments without exposing data' with compliance panel.

End of scratchpad."
